what_the_census_does_and_does_not_show: Behaviour B accounts for six of the eleven losses and was observable before landing on every census. No orchestrator cadence could have preserved it.

Behaviour A was preserved every time it was mirrored while it was still present. The five 'unknown' losses all landed before the first mirror pass of the book ran; had the mirror run during those executions, some might have been saved. That is the part of this loss the orchestrator's own cadence can be held accountable for.
No mechanism is inferred. Two A transcripts and six B transcripts came from agents given the same model and effectively the same brief.
consequence: For the writer wave, OW-6 stage-1 transcript auditors can read four of fifteen runs. Every deliverable and every OW-8 layer-C record survives. Under OW-8 this is an evidence gap, not a defect and not a stop condition. How the whole-book final audit of a HARD book carries it is routed to the controlling agent as queue item Q8 (sp_durable/Ezek/ezek_controlling_agent_queue.v1.json).
control_status: unchanged from v2: mirror on every landing and during runs (preserves A); classify each running execution as A or B on every census; a runtime-capture change is the only remedy for B and remains the separate open owner decision under OW-8(f).
